title: Trans Saharan Slave Trade
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Handle with care and link to today's rights. Facts: camel caravans with guides crossed the Sahara between West and Central Africa and North Africa, stopping at oases.

skills.key_step: The child says how the Trans-Saharan slave trade began, how it was organised and its effects.

floor.prerequisite: Locates the key features of Africa.
floor.question: Which is the largest hot desert in Africa?

steps: Name the people who ran it.

board.do: Draw the Sahara with a line of camels crossing it.
Wait for "they survive long without water".
Write two factors and two effects.

misconceptions.ask: How did traders cross the Sahara?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what travels over a desert.

misconceptions.ask: Which factor helped the Trans-Saharan trade grow?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what the traders had to cross the desert.

misconceptions.ask: Which was an effect of the Trans-Saharan slave trade?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens to a village when its young people are taken.

misconceptions.ask: Why did caravans stop at oases?
misconceptions.repair: Show an oasis photo and the route linking them.

checks.question: How did traders cross the Sahara?
Give one effect of the Trans-Saharan slave trade.
checks.answer: any of: loss of people, broken families, emptied villages, wars and raids
